column1: # libaom palette-mode ablation — isolates how much of the zenrav1e-vs-libaom RD gap
# (docs/RD_GAP_VS_LIBAOM.md) is specifically attributable to palette mode, which zenrav1e's
# encoder does not implement at all (write_use_palette_mode is hardcoded enable=false,
# unreachable!() if called with true; zenrav1e#2 tracks it). Same aomenc settings/corpus as
# the 2026-06-30 baseline, run TWICE per (image,cq): default (--enable-palette=1, implicit)
# vs --enable-palette=0. Format 420 only. cpu-used=2. 22/22 images (o_7002 also captured
# separately at matched-cq, see below).
# Harness: scripts/rd_gap/palette_ablation.sh + analyze_palette_ablation.py (zenavif bcb3874fbb92).
# libaom: git 632172a4 (aomenc 3.14.1). Scorer: fast-ssim2-cli v0.6.0.
# + = disabling palette costs MORE bits (i.e. palette was helping libaom).
# PHOTOS (families 1,2,3,5,6,8,9; matched-ssim2 frontier comparison, n=18 at ssim2 82):
target_ssim2
# -> Palette is a NO-OP for this photo corpus: libaom's own RDO essentially never selects
#    palette mode on photographic content in this cq range, so zenrav1e's missing palette
#    support does NOT explain the ~8-18% photo gap. (17/18 photo images bit-identical on/off;
#    family 9 showed a small +/-1-3% noise-level wobble, no consistent sign.)
# PLOTS (family 7 = 7000-lilith-plots synthetic screen content; matched-CQ comparison since
# achieved ssim2 tops out ~65-70 in this cq range, below the 82-90 photo targets; n=24 = 3
# images x 8 cq points):
target_metric
matched_cq
# -> On screen content, disabling palette costs a median +51.8% (up to +103%) more bytes at
#    essentially the SAME achieved ssim2 (median delta -0.24, i.e. disabling palette is never
#    a quality-for-rate trade here, strictly worse). Palette mode is the dominant explanation
#    for the +130-470% fam7 gap in the 2026-06-30 baseline.
# CONCLUSION: palette-mode implementation in zenrav1e would be a large, clear win for
# screen-content/synthetic AVIF encodes and ~zero measured effect on the photo gap. Priority
# depends on whether screen content is part of the target traffic mix (see RD_GAP_VS_LIBAOM.md).
